propositions: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host with an attested gate leaves its snapshot store append-only and unbounded
The snapshot store on non-review-bot hosts accumulates unclaimed entries (measured: 64,021 entries, 47.24 GiB) because the janitor's GC policy has no cadence outside the resident review-bot thread

A near-free O(1) in-process trigger check on the tail of gate resolution, paired with detached heavy GC work keyed to the snapshot store root, avoids the long-lock pitfall of prior ticket-store lock contention

The operation-linked GC trigger must share a stamped worker.lock and gc flock sidecar at the store root, allowing single-flight across worktrees and harmless overlap with the review-bot's resident janitor
The trigger decision (stat of last-pass.stamp against interval_seconds cadence) holds no ticket-store lock, never scales with entry count, and never raises into the calling gate operation
